data.title: ScienceDaily: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

data.title: ScienceDaily: Ancient Siberian tomb reveals surprising secrets of cannabis use 2,800 years ago

data.title: ScienceDaily: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
data.summary: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known for protecting chromosomes, TRF2 also helps muscle stem cells maintain their identity and regenerate injured tissue. When scientists removed the protein in mice, muscles struggled to repair themselves, and muscular dystrophy progressed dramatically faster.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue

data.title: ScienceDaily: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
data.summary: Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra-low-power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI. Their breakthrough eliminates a long-standing "dead layer" problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin. Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials' electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy

data.title: ScienceDaily: Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide
data.summary: A surprising new study suggests that where men get their protein may be linked to their testosterone levels. Researchers studying more than 2,500 men found that higher animal protein intake, particularly from dairy, was associated with lower testosterone, while plant protein was linked to higher levels. The findings raise intriguing questions about how everyday food choices might relate to male hormone levels.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide

data.title: ScienceDaily: A surprising brain difference may explain why some kids struggle with math
data.summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that children who struggle persistently with math may have underlying differences in how their brains manage problem-solving strategies. Children with developmental dyscalculia were slower to switch strategies, less responsive to changes in difficulty, and less able to improve their approach over time. Distinct patterns of brain activity were linked to these difficulties and could even predict certain math-related abilities.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A surprising brain difference may explain why some kids struggle with math

data.title: ScienceDaily: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
data.summary: Crows may be even smarter than we thought, and their brains are astonishingly fast. Researchers at the University of Tübingen discovered that crows can make visual decisions twice as quickly as humans and monkeys, taking just 235 milliseconds on average to identify the direction of moving dots while maintaining remarkable accuracy.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover

data.title: ScienceDaily: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why
data.summary: Colorectal cancer is making an alarming comeback in the United States after more than 20 years of declining rates, and the increase is no longer limited to younger adults. A major new study found rising rates across nearly every age group under 70, including older Americans who have historically benefited most from cancer screening.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why

data.title: ScienceDaily: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
data.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

data.title: ScienceDaily: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
data.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks

data.title: ScienceDaily: A new treasure map reveals where Earth's lost prehistoric life may be hiding
data.summary: A sweeping analysis of 540 million years of marine fossils has revealed surprising gaps in our understanding of Earth's ancient life. Scientists discovered that some of the greatest opportunities for finding previously unknown species lie in relatively recent geological periods, rather than the distant past. By mapping unexplored fossil-rich regions around the world, researchers have created a powerful tool to guide future excavations.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A new treasure map reveals where Earth's lost prehistoric life may be hiding

data.title: ScienceDaily: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
data.summary: Researchers have discovered that a familiar tropical butterfly actually belongs to three nearly identical species, including one previously unknown to science. Hidden ultraviolet wing patterns and DNA differences revealed the truth, leaving scientists puzzled about how the butterflies remain genetically separate despite living side by side.
